{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2020}} {{featured list}} [[File:Beatles ad 1965 just the beatles crop.jpg|upright=1.15|thumb|alt=The Beatles in 1965|[[The Beatles]] in 1965; from left to right: [[John Lennon]], [[Ringo Starr]], [[Paul McCartney]] and [[George Harrison]].]] [[The Beatles]] were an English [[Rock music|rock]] band from [[Liverpool]] who recorded hundreds of songs during their career. The group's "main catalogue"—songs released between 1962 and 1970—consists of 213 songs (four of which exist in different versions): 188 originals and 25 covers. Since [[Break-up of the Beatles|their break-up]], over 100 more songs by the group have been officially released, including live songs the group never recorded in the studio and numerous [[outtake]]s. The band also recorded several songs that remain unreleased. Often considered the most influential band of the rock era,{{cite web |last1=Unterberger |first1=Richie |title=The Beatles – Biography & History |url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-beatles-mn0000754032/biography |publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=29 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191103055952/https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-beatles-mn0000754032/biography |archive-date=3 November 2019 |url-status=live }} the group's music pioneered new [[Recording practices of the Beatles|recording techniques]] and was primarily responsible for pop music's [[Art music#Popular music|evolution into an art form]].{{sfn|Frontani|2007|p=125}} The majority of their recordings were produced by [[George Martin]], who also played and composed string arrangements on multiple songs; his influence on the group led him to be referred to as the "[[Fifth Beatle]]". Between 1962 and 1968, the Beatles released their songs in both [[Monaural|mono]] and [[stereo]] versions;{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=28, 134, 163–164}}{{cite web |last1=Boilen |first1=Bob |title=Mono Or Stereo: Which Beatles Box Is Better? |url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=112652937 |website=[[NPR]] |access-date=1 February 2020 |date=8 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191026041832/https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=112652937 |archive-date=26 October 2019 |url-status=live }} ''[[Abbey Road]]'' and ''[[Let It Be (album)|Let It Be]]'' were mixed and released only in stereo.{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Randall |title=Review: Is 'The Beatles in Mono' necessary? Yes and no. |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-beatles-mono-20140908-column.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=1 February 2020 |date=9 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180728044739/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-beatles-mono-20140908-column.html |archive-date=28 July 2018 |url-status=live }} Their songs often featured differences between the mixes and the group put the most effort into making the mono mixes. All mono mixes were remastered and released on ''[[The Beatles in Mono]]'' box set in 2009, along with the remastering of the band's entire catalogue in stereo.{{cite news |last=Eccleston |first=Danny |title=Beatles Remasters Reviewed |work=[[Mojo (magazine)|Mojo]] |date=9 September 2009 |url=https://www.mojo4music.com/blog/2009/09/beatles_remasters_reviewed.html |access-date=13 October 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091007072418/https://www.mojo4music.com/blog/2009/09/beatles_remasters_reviewed.html |archive-date=7 October 2009}} Following their signing with [[EMI]] in 1962, each member of the Beatles contributed to songwriting. Their primary songwriters were the partnership of [[John Lennon]] and [[Paul McCartney]], who composed most of the group's songs; lead guitarist [[George Harrison]] wrote 22 songs, including "[[While My Guitar Gently Weeps]]", "[[Something (Beatles song)|Something]]" and "[[Here Comes the Sun]]",{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=145: "While My Guitar Gently Weeps"; 171: "Something"; 178–179: "Here Comes the Sun"}} while drummer [[Ringo Starr]] wrote two songs ("[[Don't Pass Me By]]" and "[[Octopus's Garden]]"),{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=137, 174}} and was credited as co-writer for four others.{{efn|These consist of "[[Dig It (Beatles song)|Dig It]]", the instrumental "[[Flying (Beatles instrumental)|Flying]]", "[[Maggie May (folk song)|Maggie Mae]]" and "[[What Goes On (Beatles song)|What Goes On]]".{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=167: "Dig It"; 123: "Flying"; 166: Maggie Mae"; 67: "What Goes On"}}}} While songs written by Lennon or McCartney were always credited to "[[Lennon–McCartney]]",{{efn|This was due to an agreement the two made before the Beatles became famous.{{cite web |last=Garcia |first=Gilbert |url=http://dir.salon.com/story/ent/music/feature/2003/01/27/paul_yoko/index.html |title=The ballad of Paul and Yoko |work=salon.com |date=27 January 2003 |access-date=5 November 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619034926/http://dir.salon.com/story/ent/music/feature/2003/01/27/paul_yoko/index.html |archive-date=19 June 2009}}}} the pair wrote many songs completely separately.{{sfn|Everett|2001|p=200}} These include "[[Come Together]]", "[[Strawberry Fields Forever]]" and "[[Nowhere Man (song)|Nowhere Man]]" (Lennon){{harvnb|MacDonald|2005|pp=355: "Come Together"}}; {{harvnb|Sheff|2000|pp=153: "Strawberry Fields Forever"}}; {{harvnb|Everett|2001|p=322: "Nowhere Man"}} and "[[Hey Jude]]", "[[Let It Be (song)|Let It Be]]" and "[[Yesterday (song)|Yesterday]]" (McCartney),{{sfn|Miles|1997|pp=465: "Hey Jude"; 20: "Let It Be"; 201–204: "Yesterday"}} the last of which is one of the most covered songs of all time.{{cite web|publisher=[[Guinness World Records]] |year=2009 |title=Most Recorded Song |url=http://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/content_pages/record.asp?recordid=50867 |access-date=12 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060910071729/http://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/content_pages/record.asp?recordid=50867 |archive-date=10 September 2006 |url-status=dead}} Artists the band covered while together included [[Chuck Berry]] ("[[Roll Over Beethoven]]", "[[Rock and Roll Music (song)|Rock and Roll Music]]"),{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=34, 50}} [[Carl Perkins]] ("[[Matchbox (song)|Matchbox]]", "[[Honey Don't]]"),{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=44, 51}} [[Larry Williams]] ("[[Slow Down (Larry Williams song)|Slow Down]]", "[[Dizzy Miss Lizzy]]"){{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=44, 58}} and [[Little Richard]] ("[[Long Tall Sally]]").{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|p=41}} Cover songs were included on five of the band's core albums: ''[[Please Please Me]]'' and ''[[With the Beatles]]'' (both 1963), ''[[Beatles for Sale]]'' (1964), ''[[Help!]]'' (1965) and ''[[Let It Be (album)|Let It Be]]'' (1970).{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=32–33: ''Please Please Me''; 37: ''With the Beatles''; 53: ''Beatles for Sale''; 62: ''Help!''; 199: ''Let It Be''}} Lead vocals were also shared by the group, with Starr usually contributing vocals to one song per album.{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|p=67}} The group were known for their harmonies, mostly two-part, but sang intricate three-part harmonies on "[[This Boy]]", "[[Yes It Is]]" and "[[Because (Beatles song)|Because]]".{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|p=36: "This Boy"; 54: "Yes It Is"; 184: "Because"}} Originally rooted in [[skiffle]] and 1950s [[rock and roll]] music, the group embraced [[pop music]] in their early years ("[[She Loves You]]", "[[I Want to Hold Your Hand]]"),{{sfn|Everett|2001|p=174}} but began to branch out into different genres, including [[folk rock]] (''Help!'', ''[[Rubber Soul]]''),{{sfn|Unterberger|2002|p=272}}{{cite web |last1=Unterberger |first1=Richie |title=''Rubber Soul'' – The Beatles |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/rubber-soul-mw0000192940 |publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=21 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013145500/https://www.allmusic.com/album/rubber-soul-mw0000192940 |archive-date=13 October 2019 |url-status=live }} [[country music|country]] ("[[Act Naturally]]", "[[Don't Pass Me By]]"){{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|p=60}} and [[psychedelia]] (''[[Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band]]'', ''[[Magical Mystery Tour]]''). Their 1968 [[The Beatles (album)|self-titled album]] (also known as the "White Album") in particular featured a wide range of styles, including [[ska]] ("[[Ob-La-Di, Ob-La-Da]]"), [[blues]] ("[[Yer Blues]]"),{{sfn|Everett|1999|p=170}} [[hard rock]] ("[[Helter Skelter (song)|Helter Skelter]]" and the single version of "[[Revolution (Beatles song)|Revolution]]"),{{sfn|Winn|2009|p=210}}{{sfn|Doggett|2007|p=176}} and a [[musique concrète]] [[sound collage]] ("[[Revolution 9]]").{{sfn|Everett|2001|p=174}}{{cite web |last1=Erlewine |first1=Stephen Thomas |author-link1=Stephen Thomas Erlewine |title=''The Beatles'' [White Album] – The Beatles |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-beatles-white-album-mw0000418113 |publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=10 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120530202730/https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-beatles-white-album-mw0000418113 |archive-date=30 May 2012 |url-status=live }} The group also composed numerous [[ballad]]s, including "[[Michelle (song)|Michelle]]" and "[[The Long and Winding Road]]".{{cite web |last1=Unterberger |first1=Richie |title="Michelle" – The Beatles |url=https://www.allmusic.com/song/michelle-mt0010100270 |publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=23 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626110223/https://www.allmusic.com/song/michelle-mt0010100270 |archive-date=26 June 2019 |url-status=live }}{{cite web |last1=Unterberger |first1=Richie |title="The Long and Winding Road" – The Beatles |url=https://www.allmusic.com/song/the-long-and-winding-road-mt0010130339 |publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=23 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626110646/https://www.allmusic.com/song/the-long-and-winding-road-mt0010130339 |archive-date=26 June 2019 |url-status=live }} During their career, the Beatles introduced more innovations into popular music than any other rock band of the 20th century. Some of these include one of the first uses of guitar [[Audio feedback|feedback]] in music ("[[I Feel Fine]]"),{{sfn|Everett|2001|pp=265–266}} the first use of a [[Fade (audio engineering)|fade-in]] in a pop song ("[[Eight Days a Week]]"),{{sfn|Hertsgaard|1996|p=104}}{{sfn|Miles|2001|p=180}} use of [[tape loop]]s ("[[Tomorrow Never Knows]]"),{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|p=72}} using the [[recording studio as an instrument]] (''[[Revolver (Beatles album)|Revolver]]'' and ''Sgt. Pepper''){{sfn|Julien|2008|p=162}} and popularising the Indian [[sitar]] in pop music ("[[Norwegian Wood (This Bird Has Flown)|Norwegian Wood]]");{{sfn|Rodriguez|2012|p=69}} Harrison further embraced Indian music on songs such as "[[Love You To]]", "[[Within You Without You]]" and "[[The Inner Light (song)|The Inner Light]]".{{sfn|Lavezzoli|2006|pp=175–184}} ''[[Abbey Road]]'' (1969) featured prominent use of the [[Moog synthesiser]] and the [[Leslie speaker]], along with a medley of song fragments edited together to form a single piece.{{cite web |last1=Erlewine |first1=Stephen Thomas |author-link1=Stephen Thomas Erlewine |title=''Abbey Road'' – The Beatles |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/abbey-road-mw0000192938 |publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=21 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120529232715/https://www.allmusic.com/album/abbey-road-mw0000192938 |archive-date=29 May 2012 |url-status=live }} Along with their main catalogue, over 100 previously unreleased songs have been released on numerous live albums, compilations, and deluxe editions. These include demos, [[outtake]]s, songs the group only recorded live and not in the studio and, for ''[[The Beatles Anthology]]'' in the 1990s, two reunion songs: "[[Free as a Bird]]" and "[[Real Love (Beatles song)|Real Love]]".{{sfn|Harry|2000|pp=111–112}} A final reunion song, "[[Now and Then (Beatles song)|Now and Then]]", was released in 2023.{{cite web |last=Runtagh |first=Jordan |title=Inside the Last Beatles Song: How 'Now and Then' Brought the Fab Friends Together One Final Time (Exclusive) |url=https://people.com/the-beatles-announce-new-song-now-and-then-8382741 |website=[[People (magazine)|People]] |access-date=1 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231031213940/https://people.com/the-beatles-announce-new-song-now-and-then-8382741 |archive-date=31 October 2023 |date=26 October 2023 |url-status=live}} The Beatles remain one of the most acclaimed and influential artists in [[popular music]] history.{{cite web|last1=Kopf|first1=Dan|last2=Wong|first2=Amy X.|title=A definitive list of the musicians who influenced our lives most|url=https://qz.com/1094962/a-definitive-list-of-the-musicians-who-influenced-our-lives-most/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007163623/https://qz.com/1094962/a-definitive-list-of-the-musicians-who-influenced-our-lives-most/|archive-date=7 October 2017|website=[[Quartz (publication)|Quartz]]|date=7 October 2017|access-date=13 August 2019}} Their songs have been covered thousands of times by a wide range of artists and [[Cultural impact of the Beatles|continue to be celebrated]] around the world. ==Main songs== [[File:George Martin - backstage at LOVE.jpg|thumb|upright|alt=George Martin in 2006|[[George Martin]] (pictured in 2006) was the Beatles' primary producer, producing nearly all of their recordings. He is sometimes referred to as the "[[Fifth Beatle]]".{{cite web |last1=Dye |first1=David |title=Sir George Martin Talks 'Love' On World Cafe |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/world-cafe/2007/02/19/6665771/george-martin-the-fifth-beatle-returns |publisher=[[NPR]] |access-date=27 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702233429/https://www.npr.org/sections/world-cafe/2007/02/19/6665771/george-martin-the-fifth-beatle-returns |archive-date=2 July 2018 |date=19 February 2007}}]] Between 1963 and 1966, the Beatles' songs were released on different albums in the United Kingdom and the United States. In the UK, 30 songs were released as non-album singles, while appearing on numerous albums in the US. Since the remastering of the band's catalogue on [[CD]]s in the 1980s, the Beatles have a primary "core catalogue" of 14 albums:{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=200–201}} * ''[[Please Please Me]]'' (1963) * ''[[With the Beatles]]'' (1963) * ''[[A Hard Day's Night (album)|A Hard Day's Night]]'' (1964) * ''[[Beatles for Sale]]'' (1964) * ''[[Help!]]'' (1965) * ''[[Rubber Soul]]'' (1965) * ''[[Revolver (Beatles album)|Revolver]]'' (1966) * ''[[Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band]]'' (1967) * ''[[Magical Mystery Tour]]'' (US LP, 1967){{efn|''Magical Mystery Tour'' was released as a double [[extended play]] in the UK, featuring only the songs from [[Magical Mystery Tour (film)|the film]], and a standard LP in the US, featuring the films tracks and the group's five other 1967 singles.{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=130–131}} Eventually (in November 1976), the US version was released in the UK.{{sfn|Carr|Tyler|1978|p=121}} When remastering the Beatles' music on CD in the 1980s, EMI adopted the US LP version rather than the UK EP.{{sfn|Miles|2001|p=286}}}} * ''[[The Beatles (album)|The Beatles]]'' ("The White Album", 1968) * ''[[Yellow Submarine (album)|Yellow Submarine]]'' (1969) * ''[[Abbey Road]]'' (1969) * ''[[Let It Be (album)|Let It Be]]'' (1970) * ''[[Past Masters]]'' (compilation album, 1988){{efn|''Past Masters'' collected 25 of the Beatles' 30 non-album singles, along with the 1964 EP ''[[Long Tall Sally (EP)|Long Tall Sally]]'' and other rarities that were commercially available in the 1960s.{{sfn|Lewisohn|1988|pp=200–201}}}} {| id="toc" class="toc" summary="Class" align="center" style="text-align:center;" !
